_comment: Physical constants for the lithic fracture world. SI units. Prepared 2026-10-15 before the loop; the loop must not edit this file. Every value carries its source. 'range' gives the spread across sources; 'value' is what the code uses. Values flagged 'secondary' come from a database or a secondary citation and should be replaced by a primary source when one is found (record that as a deviation, do not edit here).

youngs_modulus_pa.source: MakeItFrom 'Annealed Soda-Lime Glass' (71 GPa, secondary); Pilkington technical bulletin ATS-129 (72 GPa, secondary)

poisson_ratio.source: TU Darmstadt thesis on glass fracture (0.22); MakeItFrom (0.23, secondary)

density_kg_m3.source: MakeItFrom 2.4 g/cm3 (secondary); Husien 2010 MSc thesis Table 3.1 lists soda lime glass 2.4 g/cm3; 2500 is the common float-glass value (secondary)

fracture_toughness_pa_sqrt_m.source: MakeItFrom 0.75 (secondary); Univ. Trento sandwiched-beam measurement 0.74 MPa m^0.5 (iris.unitn.it/handle/11572/74685). Quasi-static value; dynamic toughness rises with loading rate (Purdue dissertation AAI1490606: 0.66-2.22)

tensile_strength_pa.source: MakeItFrom UTS 41 MPa, flexural 100 MPa (secondary). Glass strength is flaw-controlled

microstructure_scale_m.source: amorphous; no grains. Order-of-magnitude network scale, assumption

hertzian_cone_included_angle_deg.source: McPherron et al. 2020 PLOS ONE 15:e0241714 (PSIA 136.49 +/- 7.56 on Dibble glass flakes; ~136 deg from fracture-mechanics refs). VALIDATION TARGET ONLY - must not be used as a model input

obsidian.role: fine-grained natural glass, excellent knapping material

youngs_modulus_pa.source: Husien 2010, Fracture behavior and mechanical characterization of obsidian, MSc thesis, Oklahoma State Univ., Table 3.6 (pulse echo 67.5 GPa; nano-indentation 56.9-61.2)

fracture_toughness_pa_sqrt_m.source: Husien 2010 Table 3.8 SEVNB black obsidian 1.31 (the same method gave soda-lime 0.58, i.e. biased low); natural obsidian 1.65 in J. Non-Cryst. Solids 2021 (S0022309321004671)

tensile_strength_pa.source: Husien 2010 Table 3.7 biaxial (ring-on-ring) strength: black 35 +/- 6.7, red tiger 56.9 +/- 11.2 MPa

microstructure_scale_m.source: amorphous volcanic glass; nanometre-scale edges are reported in the archaeological literature (assumption pending a cited edge-radius measurement)

youngs_modulus_pa.source: Kazakhstan chert UT-22, indentation estimate 77 GPa (PLOS ONE 2022, 10.1371/journal.pone.0265640); Schmidt et al. 2019 (10.1007/s12520-018-0710-y) report bar-to-bar variation up to +/-15 GPa

poisson_ratio.source: Nickel & Schmidt 2022 PLOS ONE 17:e0278643 give 0.2-0.3 for most brittle materials; no flint-specific value found (assumption)

density_kg_m3.source: ASSUMPTION: alpha-quartz/chalcedony density; no flint-specific measurement cited yet

fracture_toughness_pa_sqrt_m.source: Schmidt et al. 2019 via PLOS ONE 2022 (chert and silcrete 1.3-1.85, indentation fracture resistance); Kazakhstan chert 2.4 (indentation)

tensile_strength_pa.source: Nickel & Schmidt 2022 citing Schmidt et al. 2019: flint characteristic 4-point-bending strength 164-189 MPa at 30 mm3 effective volume; Aliyu et al. 2017 report <100 MPa

microstructure_scale_m.source: cryptocrystalline (<1 um grains), PLOS ONE 2022 Kazakhstan study

youngs_modulus_pa.source: EarthRef ERR 60452 representative intact basalt 73 GPa; Etna basalt 25 GPa (microcracked) and fresh Icelandic intrusive basalt 36 GPa (EGU2007-J-06750)

density_kg_m3.source: engineering tables give 3.00 t/m3 solid density (secondary); 2900 is a central value (assumption within range)

fracture_toughness_pa_sqrt_m.source: Balme et al. 2004 J. Volcanol. Geotherm. Res. (Icelandic basalt ~2.4, Etna ~2.2 MPa m^0.5 at STP); Atkinson & Meredith 1987 average 2.58; EarthRef 1-3

tensile_strength_pa.source: EarthRef ERR 60452 intact basalt tensile strength 14 MPa

microstructure_scale_m.source: ASSUMPTION: typical groundmass crystal size of fine-grained basalt; needs a cited value

basalt.heterogeneity: homogeneous at simulated resolution (crystals below grid scale)

youngs_modulus_pa.source: granite blast study (Springer Professional 'Internal fractures after blasting confined rock and mortar cylinders'): 65.30 +/- 0.83 GPa

fracture_toughness_pa_sqrt_m.source: Yu et al. 2018 PLOS ONE 13:e0180880 (grain 1.01 mm: 2.24; 2.12 mm: 1.91; 3 mm: 1.87); Atkinson & Meredith 1987 average 1.73

tensile_strength_pa.source: Yu et al. 2018 (9.5 MPa at 1.01 mm grain); blast study Brazilian 10.85 +/- 1.52 MPa

microstructure_scale_m.source: Yu et al. 2018 grain size 1.01 mm (paired with the toughness/strength above); blast study 1-3 mm

mosaic._comment: Grain-scale mineral mosaic. Mineral micro-parameters from Yu et al. 2018 Table 4 (RFPA micro-mechanical parameters, their ref. 41). Volume fractions are an ASSUMPTION for a typical granite; grain-boundary strength is a CALIBRATED parameter (see calibration).
mosaic.fraction_source: ASSUMPTION (typical granite modal composition); replace with a cited modal analysis if found

calibration._comment: The ONLY parameters the loop may fit. Each is fitted to a bulk material property, never to a validation target (Dibble data, cone angle, cutting data).

granite_grain_boundary_strength.target: simulated bulk tensile strength of the granite mosaic equals tensile_strength_pa of granite (9.5 MPa) within 10%
granite_grain_boundary_strength.procedure: simulated direct-tension or Brazilian test on >= 10 random mosaics (seeds 0-9); report the fitted value and its spread
